decisive_items: tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast with overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
skin fistula developed with pus extruding and an “orange peel” appearance of the overlying skin
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls throughout the gland, extending to the skin, with peripheral enhancement
response.rationale: R2 is the champion because it has the most comprehensive support from the vignette, including clinical presentation, imaging findings, and the development of a skin fistula, all of which are consistent with granulomatous mastitis. R5 is the runner-up because it also has support from the vignette, particularly the imaging findings, but it lacks some of the key clinical features that make R2 a stronger candidate.

rejected.why: R1 is rejected because, although it shares some clinical features with the vignette, such as nipple retraction and a skin fistula, it does not fully account for the imaging findings and the overall clinical presentation, which are more consistent with granulomatous mastitis.
C1 is rejected because it is an append-only completion of R5 and does not provide sufficient additional information to make it a stronger candidate than R2 or R5.
